page: Amazon Web Services m7i.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache pool. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 384.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmarks reflect high memory throughput, delivering 228.02 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block read operations and 95.54 GB/sec in large-block write operations. Network throughput is provisioned at a 38 Gbps baseline. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating networked block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark evaluations position the m7i.24xlarge in the upper tier for integer, cryptographic, and multi-core computational performance. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 86,783.08 and an encryption test result of 89,229.26, both placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core stress-ng testing reached 84,968.79, while Geekbench multi-core scored 20,311.0. The presence of AMX execution units delivers solid CPU-based LLM inference, reaching 3,034.28 tokens/sec during prompt processing on small 135M parameter models and 292.76 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models.

The m7i.24xlarge exhibits favorable cost efficiency for enterprise-scale workloads requiring broad multi-threading density combined with fast DDR5 memory bandwidth without needing dedicated accelerator silicon. The primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning I/O-heavy database workloads will depend on remote storage latencies. The hardware profile is suited for large-scale web application clusters, Redis caching nodes, microservice orchestration, enterprise compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz and 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz. Based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance integrates hardware extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and cryptographic acceleration. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 38 Gbps, with zero integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators attached. In synthetic testing, the instance placed in the top 10 percent for PassMark CPU computation and encryption processing, alongside strong multi-core Geekbench and Redis caching throughput. The balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU resource ratio and high compute density make the instance appropriate for enterprise web serving, distributed caching, software build pipelines, and CPU-bound matrix workloads.
